title: PTC India, Coal India among 10 stocks offering dividend yields of up to 10% - High-yield picks | The Economic Times
text:
High-dividend-yield stocks remain on investors’ radar for their potential to generate regular income. According to a September report by Religare Broking, these 10 companies across power, mining, finance, IT and energy offered dividend yields ranging from 3.3% to 9.7%.

PTC India topped the list with a 9.7% dividend yield. The stock was priced at Rs 151, with a P/E of 8.7. Dividend per share fell to Rs 7.80 in FY25 from Rs 14.70 in FY24.

Coal India had a 6.6% dividend yield and traded at Rs 402, with a P/E of 7.9. Dividend per share stood at Rs 25.50 in FY25, compared with Rs 26.40 in FY24.

REC offered a 6.2% dividend yield and traded at Rs 315, with a P/E of 5.3. Dividend per share rose to Rs 20.40 in FY25 from Rs 19.60 in FY24.

ONGC had a 5.8% dividend yield and traded at Rs 232, with a P/E of 6.7. Dividend per share fell to Rs 12.30 in FY25 from Rs 13.50 in FY24.

Gujarat Pipavav Port offered a 5.7% dividend yield and traded at Rs 168, with a P/E of 14.9. Dividend per share declined to Rs 7.70 in FY25 from Rs 9.60 in FY24.

Power Finance Corporation had a 5% dividend yield and traded at Rs 336, with the lowest P/E of 4.3 among the 10 stocks. Dividend per share fell to Rs 13.50 in FY25 from Rs 16.70 in FY24.

Tata Consultancy Services offered a 4.5% dividend yield and traded at Rs 2,399, with a P/E of 16.2. Dividend per share rose to Rs 124 in FY25 from Rs 109 in FY24.

HCL Technologies had a 4.1% dividend yield and traded at Rs 1,312, with a P/E of 19.6. Dividend per share fell to Rs 30 in FY25 from Rs 54 in FY24.

GAIL (India) offered a 3.5% dividend yield and traded at Rs 173, with a P/E of 11.8. Dividend per share rose to Rs 6.50 in FY25 from Rs 6 in FY24.

Petronet LNG rounded out the list with a 3.3% dividend yield. The stock traded at Rs 301, with a P/E of 10.7. Dividend per share remained unchanged at Rs 10 in FY25.
